answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the vine identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator burns for 180 runs and collects one. Because the ember index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the lagoon audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 180 answers need 180 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
